statement: A tree is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its left and right children. Print the inorder traversal - the whole left subtree, then the root, then the whole right subtree - as space-separated values. Inorder places every node between its two subtrees; on a binary search tree this order emits the values sorted ascending, a fact the next topic depends on.
constraints: Node values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: The left subtree prints 4 2 5, the root 1 follows, and the right subtree 3 closes.

hint: Recurse left, visit, recurse right - the visit line sits in the middle slot.
mistake: Visiting the root first out of habit; that is preorder and the output order shifts everywhere.
